prof_* are (4 mass bins, 18 radial bins), LOS-background-subtracted stacked surface densities (Msun/h per 128^2 patch pixel for DM/gas/star; dimensionless for y; cgs for Pe). Generator = examples/profiles.py on branch analysis/wl-tsz-bridge (git show analysis/wl-tsz-bridge:examples/profiles.py). CRITICAL CONSTANTS FROM THE GENERATOR: PIX = 6.25/128 = 0.048828125 comoving Mpc/h; R500_FAC = 0.659; BG_ANN = (2.5,3.0) Mpc/h; R_EDGES = np.geomspace(0.08,5.0,19); R_CEN = sqrt(R_EDGES[1:]*R_EDGES[:-1]); the per-halo radial coordinate is x = r_Mpch/(R500_FAC*r200_h) — i.e. r_cen is r/(0.659*r200), NOT a per-halo measured r500c. KEY ENABLING FACT: tau_patches() is a PURE SCALAR MULTIPLY of the gas surface density — tau = Sigma_gas[Msun/h per pixel] * SIGMA_T*X_E_PER_MASS*MSUN_G/(H*area_cm2) with area_cm2 = (PIX_MPCH*a/H*MPC_CM)**2, SIGMA_T=6.6524e-25, M_P=1.6726e-24, X_E_PER_MASS=0.88/M_P, MSUN_G=1.989e33, MPC_CM=3.0857e24, H=0.6774, PIX_MPCH=6.25/128. data_gaps.requested: A background-subtracted per-halo stellar mass for the SHMR panel
data_gaps.why_blocked: halo_atlas.py stores sig_tot_bg and sig_gas_bg only; there is no sig_star_bg, and m_star_200c/m_star_500c are RAW full-slab cylinder sums with no _bg variant. The DM and star backgrounds cannot be separated from sig_tot_bg with what is cached.
data_gaps.closest_alternative: Use raw m_star_200c for both BIND and truth and state the caveat on-figure. Quantified: the median total LOS background inside r200 is sig_tot_bg*npix = 3.52e12 Msun/h = 12.4% of the median raw cylinder mass 2.49e13; if the cosmic stellar share of that background is ~1%, the stellar background is ~3.5e10 = ~12% of the median m_star_200c = 2.85e11. It is common to BIND and truth and therefore largely cancels in the BIND/truth ratio, which is the validation statement. Do NOT quote absolute M_star as a physical SHMR without this caveat.

data_gaps.why_blocked: m_star_200c is a PROJECTED-CYLINDER aperture sum through the whole slab: it includes satellites, ICL, and the LOS background. There is no central/satellite decomposition in the cache.
data_gaps.closest_alternative: Present it as the aperture/total stellar content, not the central SHMR. Numerically the relation is near-linear (binned median log10 M_star,200c = [11.262 11.452 11.653 11.847 12.026 12.217 12.413 12.552] at log10 M200c = [13.1 ... 14.5], slope ~0.92 dex/dex) — a central-galaxy SHMR would have slope ~0.3-0.4 here, so mislabeling it would be a physics error. Label the axis $\log_{10} M_{\star,200c}$ and say 'aperture stellar mass (centrals + satellites + LOS)'.

Do NOT describe it as an approximate rescale. The corollary is a correction to the paper: the OLD 'r/r500c' axis was the approximate one (true r500c/r200c varies roughly 0.63-0.68 with concentration over this mass range, so the old axis carried a ~5% halo-to-halo radial misassignment). The band and the running median are trustworthy; individual points above logM = 14.1 are not. Also m_star_200c is a raw projected-cylinder sum with no background subtraction (LOS contamination ~10-12% of the median value), and it includes satellites/ICL — its slope is ~0.92 dex/dex, NOT the ~0.3-0.4 of a central-galaxy SHMR. Mislabelling it as 'the' SHMR would be a physics error.
